metadata.title: OpenClaw coding engine: from tested parts to a complete workflow
metadata.description: A development update on the experimental coding engine: what is verified, what remains unfinished, and the next end-to-end milestone.

outcome.summary: A reproducible development candidate is verified. The complete protected coding workflow and production qualification remain unfinished.

provenance.summary: AI-assisted progress summary prepared at the project owner's request from recorded development validation. Local evidence bundles are not published here; this is a project status report, not independently reproduced public evidence.

blocks.text: OpenClaw is being developed as a locally operated coding engine that can take a bounded task, work in an isolated copy of a project, evaluate the result and return changes for review. The current implementation has project tracking, reporting, scoped workflow and authority mechanisms, plus experimental execution infrastructure. It is not yet a generally autonomous coding service.

blocks.label: Current status
blocks.text: An earlier review candidate is verified. Subsequent integration changes still need a refreshed release package. The next milestone is one controlled coding task that succeeds end to end, with failure and cancellation behavior demonstrated as well.

items.label: Offline validation
items.value: 1,587 tests ran with no unexpected failures. One historical expected failure and 17 explicitly excluded machine-specific checks remain.

items.label: Reproducible source
items.value: Two source exports and a reexport from extracted files were byte-identical. File hashes and sizes were checked.

items.label: Execution experiments
items.value: Disposable fixtures exercised launch settings, sealed executable bytes, bounded output, deadlines, same-group child cleanup and Windows-to-Linux handoff.

items.label: Release preparation
items.value: An offline demo, portable Python package, MIT license, upstream notices, documentation and CI configuration are prepared.

blocks.text: These are recorded development results, not proof of an accepted production deployment. The offline suite did not repeat the consumed native experiments. The package demonstrates offline behavior; it does not install a fully operational coding service. The engine source has not yet been published as a GitHub release.

Three executor gaps were reproduced with disposable test processes and corrected. A child closing both output streams no longer disables its deadline. Interrupting capture now stops and reaps the direct child before the original interruption returns to the caller. A pipe held open outside the stopped process group can no longer keep cleanup waiting indefinitely: an incomplete read is reported as an execution error.

That executor snapshot passed a full offline run of 1,591 tests with no unexpected failures, errors or skips. One historical expected failure and 17 explicitly excluded machine-specific checks remain. The tested source hashes were checked at the time of validation. Focused validation also passed 79 checks covering the new regressions and existing execution and one-shot authority behavior.

A separate Windows-to-Linux development fixture also passed two cases after a child and grandchild confirmed they were running: an explicit cancel message, and closure of the input connection. Linux reported the direct child reaped by the executor, the grandchild reaped after termination, and no remaining children. The host observed completion in 247 ms and 211 ms. This is cooperative cancellation evidence for that disposable workload, not proof for forcibly killing the Windows launcher or for descendants that escape containment.

blocks.label: Scope of this result
blocks.text: These corrections are local development changes and are not included in the earlier release-preparation archive. Complete cross-host cancellation, escaped-descendant containment, production qualification and a real coding task remain unfinished.

sections.title: Keeping a result when the requester disappears

blocks.text: Forcibly terminating the Windows requester exposed a gap: the known Linux processes disappeared, but no completion report survived. That experiment remains inconclusive. A separate backend was then tested so the work and its reporting could outlive the requester's connection.

In the latest disposable experiment, Windows terminated the requester after the worker confirmed readiness. The backend detected the disconnect, requested cancellation, confirmed direct-child and grandchild cleanup, and saved a terminal execution-failure result. A separate process reopened the store and read that result. Windows termination took 282 ms; the worker reported completion in 113 ms. These are observations from one experiment, not performance guarantees.

The executor now accepts an explicit cancellation signal and returns a failure observation that the existing task pipeline can save. Focused validation passed 82 execution and authority checks plus a pipeline test showing a persisted failure and no replay launch. A broader pipeline run passed 179 of 182 tests; the other three failed because installed Python or standard-library bytes did not match pinned runtime requirements. Those exact checks were already excluded from the offline profile. Their failures remain unresolved runtime qualification work.

blocks.label: What this establishes
blocks.text: The backend experiment and pipeline regression exercise separate boundaries. They do not yet prove a complete authenticated coding service, service restart recovery, concurrent request handling or containment of escaped descendants. The earlier 1,591-test full-suite result predates explicit cancellation. Current changes are not included in the older release archive.

items.title: Bind and claim the task once
body: Bind the exact task, source, allowed actions and deadline to a protected request. Reuse the existing transactional authority and broker mechanisms, including the existing replay rejection, rather than introduce another authority store. Lost responses and restarts must not cause another execution.

items.title: Contain execution and make stopping reliable
body: Connect the supervisor to the protected runtime and disposable workspace. Test output limits, failures, timeouts and cancellation across Windows and Linux, including cleanup of the work it started.

items.title: Demonstrate a real change
body: Use a copied test project for a small coding task. Capture the proposed change and its test result while preserving the original. Show a successful run, a deliberate failure and a cancellation.

items.title: Prepare the experimental release
body: Repeat setup from a clean environment, publish reproducible instructions and document exactly which capabilities were demonstrated. Production readiness will not be inferred from a passing prototype.

blocks.text: Authenticated task delivery, protected execution identity, final runtime integration, complete cross-host cancellation and actual dynamic-runtime qualification remain unfinished. Successor policy acceptance and the controlled project demonstration are separate gates. No live qualification or independent acceptance is claimed.
The current convergence work uses a population of one. Broader evolutionary search is a later capability, not a feature established by this milestone.

Updates will distinguish implemented behavior, recorded test results and future work. A stage counts as complete only when its actual workflow has been checked. This public log contains a sanitized summary rather than local paths, private logs, raw manifests or internal authority records.
